solution: With cube edge \(a\), the cuboid is \(3a \times a \times a\): surface area \(2(3a^2 + a^2 + 3a^2) = 14a^2\). The three cubes have \(3 \times 6a^2 = 18a^2\). Ratio \(14 : 18 = 7 : 9\).
The volume scales by \(1.12^3 = 1.404928\), an increase of about 40.5%.
154 g of water is \(154 \text{ cm}^3\). \(\frac{22}{7} \times 3.5^2 \times h = 38.5h = 154\), so \(h = 4\) cm.
\(\frac{\pi r^2 h}{2\pi rh} = \frac{r}{2} = \frac{924}{264} = 3.5\), so \(r = 7\) m and the diameter is 14 m.
Slant height \(= \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = 25\) m. Canvas \(= \pi rl = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 25 = 550 \text{ m}^2\). At 50 m wide, the length is \(\frac{550}{50} = 11\) m.
The volume of a cone is proportional to its height, so doubling the height doubles the volume, an increase of 100%.
Surface areas \(4 : 25\) mean radii \(2 : 5\), so the volumes are \(2^3 : 5^3 = 8 : 125\).
Cone : cylinder \(= \frac{1}{3}\pi (2r)^2 h : \pi r^2 h = \frac{4}{3} : 1 = 4 : 3\).
The cylinder holds \(\pi \times 3^2 \times 32 = 288\pi\). Then \(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 288\pi\) gives \(R^3 = 216\) and \(R = 6\) cm.
With slant height \(R\), \(S = \pi R \cdot R + \pi R^2 = 2\pi R^2\). The circle of radius \(2R\) has \(A = 4\pi R^2 = 2S\).
In 5 s it makes \(5 \times 5 = 25\) rounds, each covering 60 cm: \(25 \times 60 = 1500\) cm \(= 15\) m.
Volume is kept: \(R^3 = 27 \times 0.2^3\), so \(R = 3 \times 0.2 = 0.6\) cm.

Cylinder: \(r = 63\), \(h = 5\), curved surface \(2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 63 \times 5 = 1980\). Cone: height \(21 - 5 = 16\), slant \(\sqrt{63^2 + 16^2} = 65\), curved surface \(\frac{22}{7} \times 63 \times 65 = 12870\). Canvas \(= 14850 \text{ m}^2\), costing \(14850 \times 12 = 178200\) rupees.
The sphere holds \(\frac{4}{3}\pi \times 216 = 288\pi\). The hollow cylinder holds \(\pi(25 - r^2) \times 32\), so \(25 - r^2 = 9\) and the inner radius is 4 cm. The thickness is \(5 - 4 = 1\) cm.

Cylinder: \(2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 3 = 264\). Cone: height \(13.5 - 3 = 10.5\), slant \(\sqrt{10.5^2 + 14^2} = 17.5\), curved surface \(\frac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 17.5 = 770\). Area \(1034 \text{ m}^2\), cost \(1034 \times 2 = 2068\) rupees.

With cylinder height \(H\): \(225\pi H + \frac{2}{3}\pi \times 3375 = 225\pi H + 2250\pi = 32400\pi\), so \(H = 134\) cm. The container's height is \(134 + 15 = 149\) cm, which lies only in \(135 < h < 150\).
With \(r = 3k\), \(h = 4k\): \(\frac{1}{3}\pi (9k^2)(4k) = 12\pi k^3 = 96\pi\), so \(k = 2\): \(r = 6\), \(h = 8\), slant 10. Lateral surface \(= \pi \times 6 \times 10 = 60\pi \text{ cm}^2\).
The number is the ratio of volumes, \(\left(\frac{8}{1}\right)^3 = 512\).
Each pillar's curved surface is \(2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 0.35 \times 4 = 8.8 \text{ m}^2\); ten pillars make \(88 \text{ m}^2\), costing \(88 \times 5 = 440\) rupees.
The bucket is a frustum: \(V = \frac{\pi h}{3}(R^2 + r^2 + Rr) = \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{40}{3} \times (1225 + 196 + 490) = \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{40}{3} \times 1911 = 80080 \text{ cm}^3\).
Wetted surface \(=\) base \(+\) wall up to 4 m: \(\frac{22}{7} \times 3.5^2 + 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 4 = 38.5 + 88 = 126.5 \text{ m}^2\).
The shell holds \(\frac{4}{3}\pi(4^3 - 2^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi \times 56\). The cone of radius 4 holds \(\frac{1}{3}\pi \times 16 \times h\). Equating, \(16h = 224\) and \(h = 14\) cm.
Surface area is proportional to the square of the diameter, so doubling the diameter makes it four times as large.
Wetted surface \(=\) floor \(+\) walls up to 1.25 m: \(6 \times 4 + 2(6 + 4) \times 1.25 = 24 + 25 = 49 \text{ m}^2\).
Outer surface \(2\pi \times 3 \times 10 = 60\pi\), inner surface \(2\pi \times 2 \times 10 = 40\pi\), and two ring ends \(2\pi(3^2 - 2^2) = 10\pi\). Total \(110\pi\).

The hemisphere's curved surface is \(2\pi \times 3^2 = 18\pi\); the cone's slant height is \(\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\), curved surface \(\pi \times 3 \times 5 = 15\pi\). Total \(33\pi = 33 \times 3.14 = 103.62 \text{ cm}^2\).
\(2\pi rh = \frac{1}{3}(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2)\) gives \(3h = h + r\), so \(r = 2h = 18\) m.
Volumes \(8 : 1\) mean radii \(2 : 1\), so the surface areas are \(4 : 1\).
The pit gives \(5 \times 4 \times 2 = 40 \text{ m}^3\) of earth, spread over \(120 - 20 = 100 \text{ m}^2\): a rise of 0.4 m \(= 40\) cm.
The cube displaces \(9^3 = 729 \text{ cm}^3\); over a base of \(15 \times 12 = 180 \text{ cm}^2\) the level rises \(\frac{729}{180} = 4.05\) cm.
The largest sphere has radius 1.5 m, volume \(\frac{4}{3}\pi \times 3.375 = 4.5\pi\). The solid left is \((27 - 4.5\pi) \text{ m}^3\).

solution: In half an hour the water travels 5 km \(= 5000\) m along a pipe of section \(40 \text{ cm}^2 = \frac{1}{250} \text{ m}^2\): \(20 \text{ m}^3\). Over a base of \(80 \times 40 = 3200 \text{ m}^2\) the level rises \(\frac{20}{3200} \text{ m} = \frac{5}{8}\) cm.
Four balls of radius 1 displace \(\frac{16}{3}\pi\). Over the jar's base \(\pi \times 5^2 = 25\pi\) the level rises \(\frac{16}{75}\) cm.
Volumes \(1 : 27\) mean heights \(1 : 3\), so the small cone is 10 cm tall. The cut is \(30 - 10 = 20\) cm above the base.
With radius \(r\) and height \(2r\), the block is \(2\pi r^3\) and the sphere \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Wasted \(= \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\), so used : wasted \(= \frac{4}{3} : \frac{2}{3} = 2 : 1\).

A plane tilted \(30^\circ\) to the cross-section cuts an ellipse whose area is the circle's area divided by \(\cos 30^\circ\): \(\frac{\pi \times 1.5^2}{\sqrt{3}/2} = \frac{2.25\pi \times 2}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{3\sqrt{3}\pi}{2} \text{ cm}^2\).
The inscribed cone has radius and height \(r\): \(C = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3\), while \(H = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\). So \(C : H = 1 : 2\).
The cross-section scales by \(0.9^2 = 0.81\), so the length must scale by \(\frac{1}{0.81} \approx 1.235\), an increase of about 23%.

The cylinder (radius \(r\), height \(2r\)) is \(2\pi r^3\); sphere \(S\) has radius \(r\) and volume \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). The rest, \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3\), gives \(R^3 = \frac{r^3}{2}\). So \(r : R = 2^{1/3} : 1\).

Revolving a square of side \(r\) about a side makes a cylinder of radius \(r\) and height \(r\), total surface \(2\pi r \cdot r + 2\pi r^2 = 4\pi r^2\). The sphere's surface is also \(4\pi r^2\), so \(A = S\).
The rise displaces \(24 \times 15 \times 0.01 = 3.6 \text{ m}^3\), which is \(\frac{3.6}{0.1} = 36\) men.
The reservoir holds \(3 \times 200 \times 100 \times 12 = 720000 \text{ m}^3 = 72 \times 10^7\) L. The town uses \(50000 \times 20 = 10^6\) L a day, so it lasts 720 days.

Equal bases and volumes make the cone 3 times as tall, \(3h\). Then \(\frac{\pi r\sqrt{r^2 + 9h^2}}{2\pi rh} = \frac{15}{8}\), so \(r^2 + 9h^2 = \frac{225}{16}h^2\), \(r^2 = \frac{81}{16}h^2\) and \(r : h = 9 : 4\).

Sides \(k, 2k, 4k\) give volume \(8k^3\), so the cube's edge is \(2k\). Diagonals: \(\sqrt{1 + 4 + 16}\,k = \sqrt{21}\,k\) and \(2\sqrt{3}\,k = \sqrt{12}\,k\). Ratio \(\sqrt{\frac{21}{12}} = \sqrt{1.75}\).
The tank gives \(10 \times 7.5 \times 6 = 450 \text{ m}^3\) of earth, spread over \(125 \times 15 - 10 \times 7.5 = 1800 \text{ m}^2\): a rise of 0.25 m \(= 25\) cm.
The small cone is similar to the original with scale \(1 : 2\), so the volumes are \(2^3 : 1 = 8 : 1\).
The cube's edge is the sphere's diameter \(2r\): \(\frac{8r^3}{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3} = \frac{6}{\pi}\).

The remaining solid has the cylinder's curved surface \(2\pi \times 3 \times 4 = 24\pi\), one flat base \(9\pi\), and the cone's inner surface: slant \(\sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\), \(\pi \times 3 \times 5 = 15\pi\). Total \(48\pi \text{ cm}^2\).
Each turn of a 0.5 cm wire covers a 0.5 cm band, so the wire's length times 0.5 cm equals the curved surface: \(\frac{1000}{0.5} = 2000\) cm \(= 20\) m.
Earth removed \(= 250 \times 500 = 125000 \text{ cm}^3\). Over \(50 \times 50 = 2500 \text{ cm}^2\) the depth is 50 cm \(= 0.5\) m.
Revolving about the 7 cm side makes a cylinder of radius 4 cm and height 7 cm: \(\frac{22}{7} \times 16 \times 7 = 352 \text{ cm}^3\).
\(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\) gives \(h = 4r = 2d\), so height : diameter \(= 2 : 1\).
Sides \(6k, 3k, k\): surface \(2(18 + 3 + 6)k^2 = 54k^2 = 6a^2\), so the cube's edge is \(3k\). Volumes: \(27k^3 : 18k^3 = 3 : 2\).
Metal \(= \frac{2}{3}\pi(5^3 - 4^3) = \frac{122\pi}{3} \text{ cm}^3\); at 9 g per \(\text{cm}^3\) it weighs \(366\pi\) g.
With ball radius \(a\), the tank has radius and height \(4a\). The empty upper half is \(\pi(4a)^2 \times 2a = 32\pi a^3\); each ball is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi a^3\). So \(\frac{32}{4/3} = 24\) balls.
All three share radius \(r\) and height \(r\): cylinder \(\pi r^3\), hemisphere \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\), cone \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^3\), in the ratio \(3 : 2 : 1\).

Curved surface \(2\pi \times 8 \times 15 = 240\pi\), one flat base \(64\pi\), and the cone's inner surface with slant \(\sqrt{64 + 225} = 17\): \(\pi \times 8 \times 17 = 136\pi\). Total \(440\pi \text{ cm}^2\).

Volumes go as the cube of the radius; the original is \(1^3 = 1\) unit. I: \(8 \times 0.5^3 = 1\), exactly enough. II: \(0.75^3 + 0.8^3 = 0.422 + 0.512 = 0.934 < 1\), so both shots can be made. Both are correct.
For edges \(l, b, h\) meeting at a corner, \(V = lbh\) and \(S = 2(lb + bh + hl)\). Both statements are correct.
Two vertices are joined by an edge (1 cm), a face diagonal (\(\sqrt{2}\) cm) or a space diagonal (\(\sqrt{3}\) cm). All three occur.

I: eight drops of radius \(r\) make one of radius \(2r\); \(8 \times 4\pi r^2 = 32\pi r^2 > 16\pi r^2\). II: \(V \propto r^3\) and \(S \propto r^2\), so \(V^2 \propto r^6 \propto S^3\). III: of all solids with a given surface area the sphere encloses the most volume. All three are correct.
Cutting at the mid-point of the axis leaves a top cone of half the size, \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the volume. The frustum is \(\frac{7}{8}\), so original : frustum \(= \frac{8}{7}\).
The top circle has half the base radius, 2.5 cm: area \(\pi \times 2.5^2 = \frac{25\pi}{4} \text{ cm}^2\).
The small top cone has \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the original curved surface (scale \(\frac{1}{2}\)), so the frustum has \(\frac{3}{4}\). The ratio is \(4 : 3\).
Slant height \(= \sqrt{9^2 + (6 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{90} = 3\sqrt{10}\) cm.
The removed top cone has height \(t\) with \(\frac{t + 9}{t} = \frac{6}{3}\), so \(t = 9\) and the whole cone is \(9 + 9 = 18\) cm tall.
Total surface \(= \pi(R + r)l + \pi R^2 + \pi r^2 = \pi \times 9 \times 3\sqrt{10} + 36\pi + 9\pi = 9\pi(3\sqrt{10} + 5) \text{ cm}^2\).
